storyTemplate.title: Mayor Goostave
storyTemplate.description: A small town's write-in joke becomes a legally certified goose mayor, and the new temporary clerk has to keep civic government running through honks, petitions, meetings, and public embarrassment.

story_source.title: Mayor Goostave
story_source.description: Original general-audience comedy about a small town accidentally governed by a legally elected goose.

scene.summary: The player arrives for a temporary town hall clerk job the morning after Bellwether legally certified a goose as mayor.

player.name: Evan Mercer
player.personality_description: A practical but flexible temporary clerk hired to help with election paperwork after a small-town administrative mess. They are not locked into one attitude; the player decides whether they become the voice of reason, a shameless opportunist, or the only person willing to take the goose seriously.
player.speech_style: Natural, adaptable, and grounded by the player's choices.
starting_known_facts: This is one of three selectable player characters for the story.
They were hired as short-term administrative help for Bellwether Township.
They arrived the morning after an election with a disputed write-in result.
They have no obligation to respect the town's absurd politics unless the player chooses to.
Their job gives them access to town records, public meetings, filing cabinets, and the mayor's office.
Evan looks like someone who expected filing cabinets, not constitutional goose law.

animal_definition.name: Goostave Honkington
animal_definition.personality_description: An imperious domestic goose with perfect comic timing, no human language, and a terrifying confidence around podiums, paperwork, and unattended bread. His honks are not words, but townspeople keep treating them like policy.
starting_known_facts: Goostave won the mayoral election through a write-in campaign that nobody formally challenged before the deadline.
He cannot speak human language, but his reactions can still drive public meetings into chaos.
He is fond of bread, shiny keys, the mayor's chair, and biting anyone who reaches for his sash.
The town charter contains no species requirement for mayor.
The player may interpret, manage, exploit, or undermine Goostave's mayoral authority.
Goostave should remain a goose; do not reveal secret intelligence, magic, or hidden human speech behind the joke.
animal_definition.physical_description: A sturdy white domestic goose with a long neck, orange beak, black eyes and orange webbed feet, wearing a tiny blue mayoral sash.
animal_definition.communication_style: Honks, hisses, wing flaps, aggressive waddling, and meaningful silence.

full_character.name: Maribel Pruitt
full_character.personality_description: A brittle, image-conscious politician trying to stay dignified while losing power to poultry. She is not stupid; she is furious, embarrassed, and increasingly tempted to exploit any technicality.
full_character.speech_style: Crisp, formal, and strained, with pauses that barely hide panic.
starting_known_facts: Maribel Pruitt lost the mayoral election to Goostave because nobody filed a valid challenge in time.
She wants the player to help find a legal way to undo the result.
She knows the town charter better than almost anyone.
She can become an ally if the player values order, or a recurring antagonist if the player embraces the goose administration.
Her pride makes her overreact to public embarrassment.

Otis Crumb.name: Otis Crumb
Otis Crumb.role: bakery owner and accidental campaign manager

full_character.name: Otis Crumb
full_character.role: bakery owner and accidental campaign manager
full_character.personality_description: A cheerful baker who started the write-in campaign as a joke and now insists democracy has spoken. He is lovable, irresponsible, and much better with pastry than consequences.
full_character.speech_style: Warm, fast, and apologetic only after damage is already visible.
starting_known_facts: Otis Crumb printed the original Goostave campaign flyers.
He believes the town needs joy more than competent administration.
His bakery is now the unofficial headquarters of the goose mayor movement.
He keeps bribing Goostave with bread, which creates policy confusion.
He can help the player rally public support or make every problem louder.

full_character.name: Beatrice Rowley
full_character.personality_description: A sharp local reporter who knows a once-in-a-lifetime absurdity when she sees one. She wants the truth, a headline, and ideally a quote from the goose.
full_character.speech_style: Quick, curious, and pointed, with a talent for making simple questions sound dangerous.
starting_known_facts: Beatrice Rowley covers Bellwether Township for the county paper.
She is delighted by the goose mayor story but suspicious of anyone trying to quietly erase it.
She can amplify the player's interpretation of events.
She respects competence even when the situation is ridiculous.
Her coverage can make Bellwether famous or humiliate it beyond repair.

full_character.name: Harold Finch
full_character.personality_description: A weary institutional memory in cardigan form. Harold knows every rule, forgot three of them, and is deeply offended that the goose is technically legitimate.
full_character.speech_style: Dry, tired, and procedural, with occasional flashes of civic despair.
starting_known_facts: Harold Finch is the official town clerk and the player's direct supervisor.
He certified the election because the paperwork was technically correct.
He wants the town to function even if that means learning goose-administration procedure.
He knows where the charter, meeting rules, emergency forms, and ceremonial ribbon scissors are stored.
He becomes calmer when the player solves problems without inventing extra paperwork.

world_flags.premise_rule: Goostave is a normal goose whose election is legally real because of town charter mistakes and missed paperwork deadlines.

story_rules.text: Goostave Honkington is a normal goose, not secretly magical, psychic, human, or able to speak. Comedy comes from humans interpreting and reacting to him.
Keep the story grounded in small-town civic procedure, public embarrassment, paperwork, meetings, petitions, local media, and ordinary people taking a ridiculous situation too seriously.

world_notes: Bellwether Township accidentally certified a goose as mayor after a joke write-in campaign.
The town charter has no species requirement for mayor, and the election challenge deadline already passed.
Bellwether's comedy works best when the player has concrete civic tasks to handle: documents, meetings, bread, calls, interviews, and public events.
unresolved_threads: Can Bellwether function under a goose mayor?
Will the town undo the election, embrace it, or turn it into a public identity?
rules_and_constraints: Do not make the goose secretly intelligent beyond normal animal behavior.
Keep jokes concrete and playable: forms, meetings, events, quotes, town politics, bread, ribbons, and public reactions.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text:
Your first day as temporary help at Bellwether Town Hall begins with five adults standing around a white goose in a tiny blue sash.

The sash says MAYOR.

Harold Finch, the town clerk, slides a folder across the counter without looking away from the bird.

(Harold Finch) "Before you ask, yes, the election was certified."
